headline: Over 4,800 UAE cancels visas of Bangladeshis, leaving thousands stranded
summary: Many expatriates returned to Bangladesh on leave and found their visas cancelled without warning, leaving them unable to return to their jobs and businesses in the UAE.
details: The United Arab Emirates has cancelled the visas of approximately 4,800 Bangladeshis, leaving many stranded at home after returning on leave.
Affected individuals reported receiving cancellation notices via email or mobile messages between July and September, often without any explanation or reason provided.
Some returnees, with no criminal record or legal issues, have expressed their financial devastation, as some had businesses and shops in the UAE.
On September 7, around 350 affected expatriates gathered at the National Press Club to demand rehabilitation and financial assistance from the government.
Their demands include monthly assistance of Tk 15,000-20,000 and government help in finding employment in other countries if returning to the UAE is the not possible.
State Minister for Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment Nurul Haque Nur confirmed that the ministry and foreign ministry are working to resolve the matter diplomatically.

MS Shekil Chowdhury, chairperson of the Centre for Non Resident Bangladeshi, suggested that increased scrutiny of documents, social media activities, and procedural lapses may be be influencing the cancellations.
Bangladesh has a significant expatriate population in the UAE, with more than 12 lakh Bangladeshis currently living there.
caption:

Their demands include monthly assistance of Tk 15,000-20,000 and government help in finding employment in other countries if returning to the UAE is the not possible.

State Minister for Expatriates’ Welfare and Overseas Employment Nurul Haque Nur confirmed that the ministry and foreign ministry are working to resolve the matter diplomatically.

MS Shekil Chowdhury, chairperson of the Centre for Non Resident Bangladeshi, suggested that increased scrutiny of documents, social media activities, and procedural lapses may be be influencing the cancellations.

headline_marked: City polls: [[Jamaat picks Selim Uddin and Shadik Kayem]] for Dhaka mayors
headline: City polls: Jamaat picks Selim Uddin and Shadik Kayem for Dhaka mayors
summary: The party has named Selim Uddin for Dhaka North and Ducsu VP Shadik Kayem for Dhaka South City Corporation elections.
details: Jamaat-e-Islami has unofficially announced its mayoral candidates for the upcoming Dhaka City Corporation elections.
Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar announced the names during an event at the Diploma Engineers' Auditorium in the capital.
Mohammad Selim Uddin, the Amir of Dhaka North, will contest the Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) election.
Shadik Kayem, the Vice President (VP) of the Dhaka University Central Students' Union (Ducsu), will be the candidate for Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC).
Selim Uddin is a member of the party's central executive council and a former central president of the student wing, Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir.
Shadik Kayem played a significant role as a coordinator during the 2024 mass uprising and was elected as the Ducsu VP in September 2025.
Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar also clarified that while an 11-party alliance was formed for the national election, each party will field its own candidates for the local government elections.
caption:
Jamaat-e-Islami has named its mayoral candidates for the Dhaka city polls.

Jamaat-e-Islami has unofficially announced its mayoral candidates for the upcoming Dhaka City Corporation elections.

Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar announced the names during an event at the Diploma Engineers' Auditorium in the capital.

Mohammad Selim Uddin, the Amir of Dhaka North, will contest the Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) election.

Shadik Kayem, the Vice President (VP) of the Dhaka University Central Students' Union (Ducsu), will be the candidate for Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC).

Selim Uddin is a member of the party's central executive council and a former central president of the student wing, Bangladesh Islami Chhatra Shibir.

Shadik Kayem played a significant role as a coordinator during the 2024 mass uprising and was elected as the Ducsu VP in September 2025.

Secretary General Mia Golam Parwar also clarified that while an 11-party alliance was formed for the national election, each party will field its own candidates for the local government elections.
